title: Shared long-term memory: groups keeping agent context together

sections.name: claim
sections.label: Claim
sections.content: A group of people can safely manage a shared long-term agent context, and the memory scales by federating rather than centralising. The owner, 2026-11-06: "Mukti-user, federated, fractal, long term memory is an important part of the future" (vignette e83f2d33). So far this is tested only at the smallest scale.

sections.name: story
sections.label: The story so far
sections.content:
Outside projects start from privacy: Family Intelligence builds a shared household memory that no outside server can read. The owner's position is the reverse order: encryption and access control belong to a layer above SRS, across repositories through a common interface, and SRS's part is meaning, authorship, and being able to split and merge (vignette 0b9b055b). Existing rulings agree: scope decision 9ec53ca2 puts permissions, storage, sync and transport outside SRS, and decision 31e9fd27 has already scheduled federation's return.

A test with two writers and one live group's memory point the same way. Adding to a shared memory already works: concurrent writes merge cleanly and a clash on one record is visible. Two things do not. A claimed author goes unchecked (SP-161), and bringing a split back can silently lose edits (SP-34). The live group shows the first with real consequences, and shows that people keep reading plain files, so any SRS layer has to leave those in place.

sections.name: parts
sections.label: The parts
sections.content:
1. What others are building.
2. Two writers on one memory: the test.
3. One live group's memory.
4. Against: what this thread must not assume.
Each part is a section below this one. The open questions are exercises in this thread and in Open exercises.

sections.name: open
sections.label: Open questions
sections.content:
Where this sits among the domains and on the roadmap. Whether signatures live on commits or on records. Where a record's home is recorded. Whether a safety rule is needed for what an agent takes from another member's record (SP-162, not yet seen in use).

The smallest next test is one live group's decision register as typed records, with its markdown page generated from them. That needs the group's agreement.
